note: Things to take up rather than attend once — a studio, a choir, a book group, a garden, a table of chess. Hand-researched: every record was checked against the organisation's own page on `lastVerified`, and none of them is sport, which has its own tab. `rhythm` is how often it runs (weekly, monthly, anytime, occasional); `commitment` is what it asks of you to start (dropin, book, term, member); `firstStep` says how to begin in the organisation's own terms. Read by the Regulars tab in js/app.js.

items.title: Cubbon Reads
items.times: Every Saturday from 9am, by tree 3265 in Cubbon Park; a group photograph and conversation at the end
items.firstStep: No booking, no forms — bring a book, a sheet to sit on and some water
items.source: Cubbon Reads · LBB · The South First
items.why: Every Saturday morning, people spread sheets under the trees in Cubbon Park and read — silently, whatever they like, on their own and yet together. Started in December 2022 by two friends, it has since spread to more than seventy cities, but the original under tree 3265 is still the one. The talking waits until the end, when whoever stays swaps recommendations.
items.hoursNote: Every Saturday from 9am, by tree 3265 in Cubbon Park; a group photograph and conversation at the end

items.title: Sunday bird walks in Lalbagh
items.times: The Birdwatchers’ Field Club meets at 7.30am at the Lalbagh Glass House on the second Sunday of each month; Bngbirds walks a different part of the city on each of the first four Sundays
items.firstStep: Turn up at the Glass House at 7.30am on the second Sunday — no membership, no fees
items.source: Birdwatchers' Field Club of Bengaluru · Bngbirds
items.why: Bengaluru has two long-running birding groups and both walk on Sunday mornings for nothing. The Birdwatchers’ Field Club gathers at the Lalbagh Glass House on the second Sunday of the month — barbets, flycatchers, cormorants on the lake — and Bngbirds covers a different quarter of the city each week. Start at Lalbagh, and within a month you will have a pair of binoculars and a list.
items.hoursNote: The Birdwatchers’ Field Club meets at 7.30am at the Lalbagh Glass House on the second Sunday of each month; Bngbirds walks a different part of the city on each of the first four Sundays

items.title: Suchitra Film Society screenings
items.times: National and international films in the Suchitra auditorium; programme on the society’s page
items.firstStep: Free entry — check the programme and turn up
items.area: Suchitra Cinema and Cultural Academy, Banashankari 2nd Stage
items.why: A film society founded by cinephiles in 1971 that grew into a cultural campus in Banashankari, and still screens Indian and world cinema in its own auditorium without charging for a seat. Pick the ones that look unlike anything at the multiplex and it becomes the city’s best standing film habit.
items.hoursNote: National and international films in the Suchitra auditorium; programme on the society’s page

items.title: French at the Alliance Française de Bangalore
items.times: In-person and online courses at every level, with DELF and DALF preparation
items.firstStep: Pick a course from the upcoming-courses page
items.why: French taught level by level on Thimmaiah Road, in person or online, with a cultural programme in the same building. A session is weeks of classes with the same small group, which is what turns wanting to learn a language into actually learning it.
items.hoursNote: In-person and online courses at every level, with DELF and DALF preparation

items.title: Pottery at Clay Station
items.firstStep: Start with a beginners’ short course; the open studio is bookable once you can work alone
items.priceNote: Course fees on the classes page
items.why: A Koramangala pottery studio running since 2009, for everyone from the curious to the professional. Short courses take a beginner to the wheel, a six-month certificate goes much further, and the community studio can be booked for your own work once you are past the basics — which is when it turns into a weekly habit.

items.title: Bangalore Chess Club
items.cadence: Weekend meetups, often in Cubbon Park
items.times: Casual meetups and weekly tournaments in parks and cafés; events and registration on the club’s site
items.firstStep: Free, no membership — register for the next meetup on the club’s site
items.area: Cubbon Park and cafés around the city
items.why: A free, open-to-all chess club that has met in the city since 2015 — after work in cafés, at weekends under the trees in Cubbon Park — with more than a thousand people on its lists. No fees, no membership, boards for anyone who turns up, and weekly tournaments when you want to find out how good you have become.
items.hoursNote: Casual meetups and weekly tournaments in parks and cafés; events and registration on the club’s site

items.title: Repair Café pop-ups in Bengaluru
items.times: Pop-up repair workshops on Sundays, in different neighbourhoods
items.firstStep: Watch for the next pop-up; bring something broken, or volunteer a skill
items.source: Repair Café International · Repair Cafe Collective India
items.why: Started in 2015 and now run as the Repair Cafe Collective India, these pop-ups bring volunteer fixers to a different neighbourhood on a Sunday, because weekends are when the volunteers are free. Mend a lamp or a mixer instead of throwing it out, and watch how it is done — the next time, you could be one of the people fixing.
items.hoursNote: Pop-up repair workshops on Sundays, in different neighbourhoods
